ai_review.summary: A superb matrix recording of the 9/11/73 show that captures a soaring China Cat Sunflower and a mystical Dark Star > Morning Dew.
ai_review.review: The Dusborne matrix delivers crystal‑clear balance between audience ambience and soundboard detail, making this performance one of the most vivid from the ’73 fall tour. Highlights include an otherworldly China Cat Sunflower, a fiery Row Jimmy/Row Johnny segue, and a transcendent Dark Star → Morning Dew (despite a brief tuning hiccup). Overall the show flows beautifully and feels like a “church service” for Deadheads.

ai_rating.rationale: Nearly all reviewers gave five stars, praising both the musical performance and the high‑quality matrix mix; only one four‑star comment noted a minor issue, resulting in an exceptional combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Loud, balanced signals with crisp clarity; audience ambience is well blended. Minor signal change makes the Morning Dew portion sound out of tune, but overall mix is considered a gold‑standard matrix.

standout_songs: Sing Your Blues Away (Let Me Sing Your Blues Away)
poor_songs: Morning Dew (tuning issue due to signal change)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows effortlessly, moving from psychedelic explorations to tight, melodic renditions; the performance feels atmospheric and “mind‑altering,” with a particularly strong second half.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s tone is praised as perfect and fanned on Dark Star, though his guitar was briefly out of tune during Morning Dew.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass is highlighted for its loud presence and “Phreak” energy throughout the mix.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s rhythm work on China Cat Sunflower is called great, adding to the song’s drive.
